title: Agent Reasoning Engine documentation system
goal: Create one coherent, navigable, source-linked manual for the supported ARE product without mixing product guarantees, research findings, historical design, or authority claims.
goal_limits: document the existing Candidate 013 product and its verified behavior
organize rather than redefine canonical terms or product authority
keep research claims bounded to their own evidence
do not publish, deploy, activate, or approve the product
original_intent: The user wants whole documentation for ARE so a reader can understand, use, integrate, operate, evaluate, and contribute to the product without reconstructing it from scattered repository artifacts.

consumer.intended_use: Learn the product, run local workflows, connect an agent, operate continuity, interpret evidence, and change the implementation while preserving its boundaries.

concepts.candidate_definition: A maintained index and linked document set that explains the supported ARE product from first use through architecture, integration, operation, evidence, and contribution.
The reader-facing documentation rooted beside the ARE implementation and versioned with its product profile.
A table that points each documented concern to the file that owns its current machine-readable contract, authority, evidence, or historical context.
A short ordered reading path for a user, operator, integrator, contributor, reviewer, or researcher.
Documentation explains and links verified product behavior but cannot approve, promote, activate, deploy, or broaden that behavior.
Product documentation may summarize a research result only with its exact evidence and qualification boundary; research rounds do not enter the supported runtime contract by being linked.

relationships: The documentation index routes each audience to an audience path.
Each product claim points through the source-of-truth map to current evidence or a machine contract.
The product manual describes Candidate 013 while the release evidence binds its exact tested closure.
Research documentation remains subordinate to its benchmark protocols and reviewed decisions.

open_questions_and_conflicts.question: Which static documentation publisher, if any, should later render the Markdown manual?
Should generated API reference be added after the hand-written product and integration contracts stabilize?

allowed_uses: Create and review the versioned Markdown manual beside the ARE implementation.
Add navigation from the implementation README.
Validate internal links, command names, product components, and open-question ownership.
Use the manual as input to later publication planning.
blocked_actions: Treat documentation prose as canonical authority when a linked machine contract owns the fact.
Present ContextBench or provider experiments as general product qualification.
Claim hosted service, deployment, live credentials, or product approval.
Publish or deploy the documentation without a separately routed effect.

checks.detail: Users, operators, integrators, contributors, reviewers, and researchers have named reading needs.
The manual covers orientation, concepts, architecture, use, integration, operation, evaluation, release, troubleshooting, contribution, glossary, and source ownership.
Prose explains current sources and grants no promotion or effect authority.
Research is linked as bounded evidence rather than product behavior.

challenge_or_refresh_route: Route material scope changes through CA2-ROUTE-DEFINE; route bounded documentation edits through CA2-ROUTE-IMPLEMENT.
claim_ceiling: Defines the candidate scope and language of the ARE documentation system only; it does not make the documents canonical or authorize publication.
